stage1_evidence_shown.label: OBJECTIVE
stage1_evidence_shown.context: To illustrate how maternal mortality audit identifies different causes of and contributing factors to maternal deaths in different settings in low- and high-income countries and how this can lead to local solutions in reducing maternal deaths.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: DESIGN
stage1_evidence_shown.context: Descriptive study of maternal mortality from different settings and review of data on the history of reducing maternal mortality in what are now high-income countries.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: SETTINGS
stage1_evidence_shown.context: Kalabo district in Zambia, Farafenni division in The Gambia, Onandjokwe district in Namibia, and the Netherlands.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: POPULATION
stage1_evidence_shown.context: Population of rural areas in Zambia and The Gambia, peri-urban population in Namibia and nationwide data from The Netherlands.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: METHODS
stage1_evidence_shown.context: Data from facility-based maternal mortality audits from three African hospitals and data from the latest confidential enquiry in The Netherlands.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
stage1_evidence_shown.context: Maternal mortality ratio (MMR), causes (direct and indirect) and characteristics.

stage1_model_output.raw: {"action":"ANSWER","answer":"no","confidence":0.85,"reason_for_action":"Audits from diverse low- and high-income settings reveal different causes and contributing factors to maternal deaths, enabling local solutions—so differences are not just rich vs poor."}

parsed.reason_for_action: Audits from diverse low- and high-income settings reveal different causes and contributing factors to maternal deaths, enabling local solutions—so differences are not just rich vs poor.

stage2_added_evidence.label: RESULTS
stage2_added_evidence.context: MMR ranged from 10 per 100,000 (the Netherlands) to 1540 per 100,000 (The Gambia). Differences in causes of deaths were characterized by HIV/AIDS in Namibia, sepsis and HIV/AIDS in Zambia, (pre-)eclampsia in the Netherlands and obstructed labour in The Gambia.
